info.title: Vanishly API
info.description:
Share secrets with links that work only once (or a few times) and then burn.

**End-to-end encryption.** Secrets are encrypted on the client (AES-256-GCM, format v1, see `public/js/vanishly-crypto.js` and docs/INTERFACE.md). The server stores only the ciphertext. The key travels in the URL fragment (`#...`), which browsers never send to the server.

Use `POST /v1/secrets` with a client-encrypted payload. For scripts without crypto, `POST /v1/share` encrypts on the server, returns the full links with the key and forgets the key.

**Authentication.** By default none: whoever knows a secret or receipt id may use it, so ids are 128-bit random values. With sign-in on (`AUTH_PROVIDER=entra` or `oidc`, see `auth` in `GET /v1/config`) creating may need a signed-in user (`AUTH_CREATE`), and a secret with `recipients` / `recipientGroups` opens only for one of them: `GET /v1/secrets/{id}`, `/reveal` and `/v1/open` answer `401 login_required` without a sign-in and `403 not_recipient` for anybody else, without using a view. Browsers use the session cookie of `/auth/login`; scripts send an access token of the provider as `Authorization: Bearer` when the server sets `AUTH_API_AUDIENCE`.

**Switches.** An operator can turn parts off (see `features` in `GET /v1/config`). Switched-off endpoints answer 404: `/v1/share` (`ENABLE_SHARE_API`), the receipt endpoints (`ENABLE_RECEIPTS`), burn (`ENABLE_BURN`). With `ENABLE_API=false` the whole API answers 404 except for the server's own pages.

post.summary: Encrypt on the server and store (for scripts)
post.description:
The server encrypts the plaintext with a fresh key, stores the ciphertext and returns the links with the key in the fragment. The key and plaintext are not stored. Prefer client-side encryption where you can.

```
curl -s -X POST https://ots.example.com/api/v1/share -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"secret":"hunter2","ttl":3600}'
```

post.summary: Take one view: returns the ciphertext
post.description: Counts one view. When no views are left the secret is deleted. With a passphrase the verifier is checked first; a wrong one does not use a view, and after PASSPHRASE_ATTEMPTS wrong ones the secret is destroyed. ENABLE_REVEAL_API=false: only this server's reveal page may call it (404 for scripts).

post.summary: Open a secret on the server (for scripts)
post.description: For scripts without crypto: send the full secret link (with the key after `#`) and, if the secret has one, its passphrase. The server checks the passphrase, takes one view, decrypts, returns the plaintext and forgets link and passphrase. Works for every secret, also those created in the web form. Like `/v1/share`, the server sees the plaintext for this one request; browsers decrypt themselves. Answers 404 with ENABLE_OPEN_API=false or ENABLE_API=false.

404.description: Unknown, viewed, burned or expired (or switched off)

410.description: Too many wrong passphrases, the secret was destroyed

422.description: `bad_key`: the key in the link does not fit; the view was used

Put "user" into "recipients" of a new secret; it is the address the person signs in with.

user.description: Sign-in address (UPN; for guests their e-mail)

mail.description: E-mail address, empty when the account has none

error.description: Machine-readable code. 404 `endpoint_disabled`: the endpoint exists but is switched off on this server; 404 `not_found`: no such path, or the secret/receipt is gone.

rule.description: With confirmation_required: the rule to confirm, the same text as the checkbox of the form (CONFIRM_TEXT or the built-in one), in the language of the request

examples.message: I confirm that this secret contains only one password: not several passwords, no user name and no links that together give access to a whole system. Send "confirmed": true to confirm.
examples.rule: I confirm that this secret contains only one password: not several passwords, no user name and no links that together give access to a whole system.

ttl.description: Seconds until the secret expires (default DEFAULT_TTL, 60 to MAX_TTL; the form offers TTL_OPTIONS)

views.description: How often it can be viewed (at most MAX_VIEWS)

confirmed.description: Required, exactly the JSON value true, when the server has CONFIRM_CHECKBOX on: you confirm the rule of the form's checkbox (`confirmation` of /v1/config). Missing, false or "true" as a string: 400 `confirmation_required`, whose `message` and `rule` state that rule in the language of the request

recipients.description: Only with sign-in on: e-mail addresses / user names who may open the secret (case-insensitive). The caller must be signed in. Empty or missing: anyone with the link

recipientGroups.description: Only with sign-in on: groups whose members may open the secret, from RECIPIENT_GROUPS (Entra: group object ids; with RECIPIENT_GROUPS=* any group id from GET /v1/groups)

verifier.description: Passphrase verifier; leave out without a passphrase

passphrase.description: Required with REQUIRE_PASSPHRASE; at least MIN_PASSPHRASE_LENGTH characters and the classes of PASSPHRASE_COMPLEXITY

receiptId.description: null when receipts are switched off (ENABLE_RECEIPTS=false)

receiptPath.description: Status page for the sender; null when receipts are switched off

restricted.description: Only for the recipients (only a recipient gets this answer for such a secret)

viewsLeft.description: 0: this was the last view, the secret is deleted

secretPath.description: While the secret can still be viewed null when ENABLE_RECEIPT_SHARE_LINK=false.

views.description: Times of the views (no IPs are stored) Empty when ENABLE_VIEW_LOG=false.

recipients.description: Number of recipients and groups; 0 = anyone with the link

viewedBy.description: Per view (same order as views): the name of the signed-in viewer with RECEIPT_SHOW_VIEWER, else null

ttlOptions.description: Expiry choices of the form (TTL_OPTIONS), in seconds

languages.description: Languages the pages are served in (LANGUAGES; built in: en, de, more via TRANSLATIONS_DIR)

defaultLang.description: Language when the visitor's choice and browser do not decide (DEFAULT_LANG)

minPassphraseLength.description: MIN_PASSPHRASE_LENGTH (0 = no minimum); enforced by the browser and by /v1/share

requirePassphrase.description: REQUIRE_PASSPHRASE=true: every secret without a passphrase is refused (false with unless-recipients; see passphraseRule)

passphraseRule.description: REQUIRE_PASSPHRASE: off, always, or unless-recipients (a secret without recipients needs a passphrase; passphrase_required otherwise)

confirmation.description: Text the sender must confirm (CONFIRM_CHECKBOX), per language; null when off

passphraseComplexity.description: PASSPHRASE_COMPLEXITY: classes the passphrase must contain; enforced by the browser and by /v1/share

groupList.description: The groups of RECIPIENT_GROUPS, only for a signed-in caller

peopleSearch.description: true with RECIPIENT_USER_GROUP: GET /v1/people suggests people

docs.description: The API reference page; only with ENABLE_API_DOCS

endpoints.description: The endpoints switched on on this server, e.g. "POST /api/v1/secrets"

bearerAuth.description: Access token of the sign-in provider for AUTH_API_AUDIENCE (only with sign-in on)

sessionCookie.name: __Host-vanishly-session
sessionCookie.description: Session of the web sign-in (`vanishly-session` without HTTPS)
